messages.content: pretend you are a sass product pricing expert. My competitor offers a one time form filing service for $99 and an annual subscription that allows unlimited updates and filings for $149. Another competitor charges $149 for a one time filing and $249 for an annual subscription that renews each year. Assume the product are similar and commodities.  how should I price my service?

function.name: calculate_dynamic_pricing
function.description: Calculates the price for a service based on the geolocation of the customer, ensuring a minimum price threshold is met. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

geolocation.description: The geolocation of the customer in the format of 'Latitude, Longitude', such as '34.0522, -118.2437'.

base_price.description: The base price for the service before location-based adjustments. This is a float type value.

minimum_price.description: The minimum price to charge regardless of the customer's location. This is a float type value.

location_multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to the base price based on customer's geolocation. A higher multiplier indicates a more expensive area. This is a float type value.

We need to respond as a SaaS pricing expert. Provide guidance on pricing strategy, considering competitor pricing, value proposition, cost structure, target market, positioning, etc. Suggest possible price points, maybe a tiered approach, maybe a freemium or usage-based model. Also mention dynamic pricing based on geolocation? But the user didn't ask for that. They want advice on how to price their service. We can propose a pricing model: e.g., base price $129 for one-time filing, $199 for annual subscription, or maybe lower to attract customers. Or we could suggest a value-based pricing: if your service offers more features, you can price higher. Or if you want to capture market share, price slightly lower. Also consider bundling, discounts for long-term commitments, usage-based pricing. Provide a recommendation: maybe $119 for one-time, $179 for annual subscription. Or maybe a tiered subscription: Basic $99, Pro $149, Enterprise $249. Also mention dynamic pricing based on location: use the function to calculate dynamic pricing. But the user didn't ask for that. They just want advice.

We can also mention that if the product is commodity-like, price competition will drive down prices.
